import numpy as np

def avg_pos(fn, name, n=10):
    ps = []
    q = None
    for _ in range(n):
        p, q = fn(name)
        ps.append(p)
    return np.mean(ps, axis=0), q

# Perception is noisy (~1 cm per call), so average multiple queries
handle_pos, handle_quat = avg_pos(sample_grasp_pose, "extruded handle of the brown square nut")
nut_center_pos, _ = avg_pos(get_object_pose, "white hollow center of the brown square nut")
block_pos, _ = avg_pos(get_object_pose, "brown square block")

# Rigid offset from nut hollow center to handle grasp pose (assume no rotation of nut during carry)
offset = handle_pos - nut_center_pos

# Grasp the nut by its handle
goto_home_joint_position()
open_gripper()
goto_pose(handle_pos, handle_quat, z_approach=0.10)
close_gripper()

# Lift
lift_pos = handle_pos.copy()
lift_pos[2] += 0.15
goto_pose(lift_pos, handle_quat)

# Target: nut center aligned above block peg; keep the same gripper orientation
target_center = block_pos.copy()
target_center[2] = block_pos[2] + 0.02
target_handle = target_center + offset
target_handle[2] = target_center[2] + offset[2] if offset[2] > 0 else target_center[2]

# Move above the peg, then insert along Z
goto_pose(target_handle, handle_quat, z_approach=0.15)
open_gripper()

# Retreat
retreat = target_handle.copy()
retreat[2] += 0.15
goto_pose(retreat, handle_quat)
goto_home_joint_position()
